model_output.verdict: A kitchen manager with restaurant experience whose recent duties need more detail.
write_up: Your resume takes a recruiter from line cook to sous chef at Alamo Street Kitchen, then to Kitchen Manager at River Walk Grill. It’s common to describe kitchen work as a list of duties, but those duties won’t stand out in a pile when a recruiter can’t tell how you ran the operation.

The 180-seat restaurant line is the strongest starting point because it gives the kitchen a scale a recruiter can recognize. Your ServSafe Manager certification also belongs here. The other River Walk Grill lines name the work, but leave questions about the staff, ordering and training.

Let’s start with the staff schedule: add how many people you schedule and which shifts it covers. Then give the ordering, inspection and training lines a concrete detail each. Your weekly inventory counts and grill and sauté stations already tell a recruiter what you did, so those can stay.

cards.line: - Run the kitchen for a 180-seat restaurant
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this. It puts a recognizable restaurant measure beside your kitchen responsibility. Use that same approach for the staff and training lines.

cards.line: - Manage the kitchen staff schedule
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can’t tell how many people or shifts the schedule covers. That matters for a kitchen manager role.
cards.example: Manage the kitchen staff schedule for [number] staff across [shifts]
cards.question: How many staff do you schedule, and which shifts does the schedule cover?

cards.line: - Order food and supplies from vendors
cards.cannot_tell: Ordering is part of the job, but this doesn’t say which items you handle or how often you order.
cards.example: Order food and supplies from vendors, including [items], [ordering frequency]
cards.question: Which items do you order, and how often?

cards.line: - Keep the kitchen ready for health inspections
cards.cannot_tell: Inspection readiness matters, but a recruiter can’t tell what you do to keep the kitchen ready.
cards.example: Keep the kitchen ready for health inspections by [inspection preparation work]
cards.question: What do you personally do to prepare the kitchen for inspections?

cards.line: - Train new line cooks
cards.cannot_tell: This names the people you train, but not what you teach them or how many you’ve trained.
cards.example: Train [number] new line cooks on [training topics]
cards.question: How many new line cooks have you trained, and what did you teach them?

cards.line: - Ran the line on busy weekend shifts
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter knows when you ran the line, but not what you handled during those shifts.
cards.example: Ran the line on busy weekend shifts, handling [line responsibilities]
cards.question: What were you responsible for while running the line on weekend shifts?

cards.line: - Helped plan seasonal menu changes
cards.cannot_tell: Your part in the menu changes is still a blank. Keep the credit at the level you held, and name what you contributed.
cards.example: Helped plan seasonal menu changes by [your contribution]
cards.question: What did you contribute to the seasonal menu changes?

fit.why: Your headline and current role point to kitchen management, with earlier sous chef and line cook work behind them.
fit.level: manager, runs a restaurant kitchen and manages the kitchen staff schedule
fit.note: Your restaurant progression and ServSafe Manager certification fit kitchen management work. Details about the staff and day-to-day operation will make your responsibilities easier to assess.
